description: Footer no longer renders the Repository or Documentation links to github.com/dariorivera/pockety
steps: Step 1: Sign in as an existing user and load any authenticated page inside the app shell
Step 2: Scroll to the footer (AppFooter) and inspect every anchor element it renders
Step 3: Assert no anchor href equals https://github.com/dariorivera/pockety or https://github.com/dariorivera/pockety#readme
Step 4: Assert no visible footer text reads Repository or Documentation

description: Sidebar footer navigation no longer contains Repository or Documentation items
steps: Step 1: Sign in and open the sidebar on any authenticated page
Step 2: Inspect the sidebar footerNavItems region
Step 3: Assert no nav item titled Repository or Documentation exists
Step 4: Assert the sidebar renders without an empty heading where those items used to be

description: Header right navigation no longer renders the Laravel starter-kit repository or docs links
steps: Step 1: Sign in and inspect the header rightNavItems region
Step 2: Assert no anchor href contains github.com/laravel/react-starter-kit
Step 3: Assert no anchor href contains laravel.com/docs/starter-kits
Step 4: Assert any header section that held only those links is gone rather than left blank

description: Comprehensive GitHub link removal sweep across footer, sidebar, and header plus a source search proving no forbidden URLs remain
steps: Step 1: Before the change, record every occurrence of github.com/dariorivera/pockety in resources/js
Step 2: Run grep for github.com/dariorivera/pockety under resources/js and app and confirm the change makes it zero matches
Step 3: Run grep for github.com/laravel/react-starter-kit under resources/js and app and confirm zero matches
Step 4: Run grep for laravel.com/docs/starter-kits under resources/js and app and confirm zero matches
Step 5: Open the app footer and verify no GitHub or book icon remains for those links
Step 6: Open the app sidebar and verify no Repository or Documentation nav item remains
Step 7: Open the app header and verify no starter-kit links remain
Step 8: Verify no footer or header section is left as an empty container or heading
Step 9: Run the frontend unit test suite and confirm app-footer.test.tsx passes
Step 10: Run the Playwright app-footer.spec.ts and app-header.spec.ts specs and confirm they pass
Step 11: Confirm the remaining footer content (app name, version, copyright) still renders
Step 12: Confirm no test still asserts one of the removed hrefs

description: Existing footer and header tests are updated to stop expecting the removed GitHub and starter-kit hrefs
steps: Step 1: Open resources/js/components/app-footer.test.tsx
Step 2: Assert it no longer queries for github.com/dariorivera/pockety or the Repository/Documentation labels
Step 3: Open tests/browser/app-footer.spec.ts and tests/browser/app-header.spec.ts
Step 4: Assert neither spec expects the starter-kit or Pockety GitHub URLs

description: Footer and header visual layout stays balanced after removing the link clusters and any now-empty sections
steps: Step 1: Sign in and navigate to the dashboard
Step 2: Take a screenshot of the footer at desktop width
Step 3: Verify the app name, version, and copyright remain aligned and readable
Step 4: Verify there is no blank right-hand column or dangling divider where the links were
Step 5: Resize to a narrow mobile viewport and take a screenshot
Step 6: Verify the footer content stacks cleanly with no overlap or clipped text
Step 7: Take a screenshot of the header at desktop width
Step 8: Verify the right side of the header still has balanced spacing with no empty gap
Step 9: Verify no orphaned heading or separator is visible in header or footer
Step 10: Verify contrast and typography of the remaining footer text are unchanged

description: Manage Balances dialog DialogContent is limited to about 85vh while title, description, and the new-balance form stay visible
steps: Step 1: Sign in and open the Accounts page
Step 2: Open Manage Balances for an account
Step 3: Inspect the DialogContent element and confirm its max height is about 85vh
Step 4: Confirm the dialog title and description are visible at the top
Step 5: Confirm the new-balance form is visible and usable without scrolling the dialog itself
Step 6: Confirm the recorded-balances list is the region with min-h-0 and overflow-y-auto
Step 7: Confirm the dialog remains vertically centered

description: Comprehensive Manage Balances scroll test with a long list reaches the first and last row and still reaches the form
steps: Step 1: Seed an account with enough recorded balance rows to exceed the viewport height
Step 2: Sign in and open Manage Balances for that account
Step 3: Verify the dialog does not exceed about 85vh
Step 4: Verify the first recorded row is initially visible
Step 5: Scroll the recorded-balances list region down to the last row
Step 6: Verify the last row becomes visible
Step 7: Scroll back up and verify the first row is reachable again
Step 8: Verify the page behind the open dialog did not scroll during list scrolling
Step 9: Verify the title and description remained visible during scrolling
Step 10: Verify the new-balance form is still reachable and submittable after scrolling
Step 11: Verify the list scrollbar appears on the list region, not on the whole page
Step 12: Take screenshots of the top and bottom of the scrolled list as evidence

description: Short recorded-balances list still fits its content without a useless scrollbar or page scroll behind the dialog
steps: Step 1: Seed an account with only two recorded balance rows
Step 2: Open Manage Balances
Step 3: Verify the dialog height fits the content and does not use the full 85vh unnecessarily
Step 4: Verify no scrollbar appears in the recorded-balances list
Step 5: Verify the page behind the dialog does not scroll
Step 6: Verify the dialog closes normally and the page is still at its previous scroll position

description: Manage Balances dialog visual constraint applies only to this dialog and preserves its layout
steps: Step 1: Open Manage Balances with a long list at desktop width
Step 2: Take a screenshot of the dialog
Step 3: Verify the dialog is centered and no taller than about 85vh
Step 4: Verify the heading and description have normal spacing and are not scrolled away
Step 5: Verify the new-balance form sits above the scrolling list and is not clipped
Step 6: Verify the list shows a visible scroll affordance when it overflows
Step 7: Verify row spacing and alignment inside the list are unchanged
Step 8: Open a different dialog in the app and confirm its DialogContent default classes are unchanged
Step 9: Verify the page behind the dialog shows no unnecessary scrollbar
Step 10: Verify the dialog at a narrow mobile width still contains the list and form without horizontal overflow

description: The shared dialog component default classes are unchanged and only Manage Balances adds the scroll constraint
steps: Step 1: Inspect resources/js/components/ui/dialog.tsx DialogContent default classes
Step 2: Assert its default max-height and overflow classes were not modified
Step 3: Inspect the Manage Balances dialog in resources/js/pages/accounts.tsx and confirm it passes its own 85vh constraint class
Step 4: Open another dialog in the app and confirm it is not constrained to 85vh

description: Each account row exposes an Edit action in the accounts list
steps: Step 1: Sign in and open the Accounts page
Step 2: Assert every account row has an Edit action
Step 3: Click Edit on an account and confirm a dialog opens
Step 4: Close the dialog and confirm the list is unchanged

description: Comprehensive account edit dialog loads values, submits PUT /api/accounts/{id}, and refreshes the list
steps: Step 1: Seed an account for the signed-in user with a known name, type, primary currency, notes, and active flag
Step 2: Sign in and open the Accounts page
Step 3: Click Edit on that account
Step 4: Verify the dialog is prefilled with the account's name, type, primary currency, notes, and active flag
Step 5: Change the name and submit
Step 6: Verify the client sends a PUT or PATCH to /api/accounts/{id}
Step 7: Verify the dialog closes on success
Step 8: Verify the accounts list refreshes and shows the new name
Step 9: Reload the page and verify the new name persisted
Step 10: Verify the other fields were not unintentionally changed
Step 11: Verify another user with the same account name is not affected
Step 12: Confirm no console or network error occurred

description: Edit dialog disables the type control and explains the lock when the account has transactions
steps: Step 1: Seed an account that has at least one transaction for the signed-in user
Step 2: Open the Accounts page and click Edit on that account
Step 3: Verify the type control is disabled
Step 4: Verify the dialog shows an explanation that the type cannot change because transactions are registered
Step 5: Verify name, primary currency, notes, and active flag remain editable
Step 6: Change the name and submit successfully
Step 7: Reopen Edit and verify the type is unchanged
Step 8: Confirm the type lock explanation is visible and readable
Step 9: Submit a forced type change and verify the 422 message is shown in the dialog
Step 10: Verify the stored type is still unchanged

description: Feature test covers both the allowed account update and the blocked type change with transactions
steps: Step 1: Create an account with a transaction for user A
Step 2: PUT a new name only and assert 200 plus the new name persisted
Step 3: Assert the type is unchanged by the successful update
Step 4: PUT a different type and assert 422
Step 5: Assert the stored type in the database is unchanged after the 422
Step 6: Create an account with no transactions for user A
Step 7: PUT a different type and assert success
Step 8: Assert the stored type changed
Step 9: PUT name, primary_currency, notes, and is_active on an account with transactions and assert success
Step 10: Assert a soft-deleted transaction still counts as a transaction for the type lock
Step 11: Assert another user's account with the same name does not collide and owner-scoped uniqueness holds
Step 12: Run php artisan test --filter the account update tests and confirm all pass

description: Account update API counts transactions for the account owner including soft-deleted transactions
steps: Step 1: Create an account for user A with one soft-deleted transaction if the model supports soft deletes
Step 2: PUT a different type that is otherwise valid and assert 422
Step 3: Assert the account type did not change
Step 4: Restore or hard-delete the transaction and repeat the type change
Step 5: Assert the type change now succeeds when no transactions remain

description: Type change is allowed when the account has no transactions
steps: Step 1: Create an account with no transactions
Step 2: PUT a valid different type
Step 3: Assert 200 and the new type persisted
Step 4: Verify the response payload reflects the new type

description: Name uniqueness remains owner-scoped after the account edit change
steps: Step 1: Create account 'Savings' for user A and account 'Savings' for user B
Step 2: As user A, update user A's account without changing the name and assert success
Step 3: As user A, attempt to rename user A's account to a name already used by user A and assert a validation error
Step 4: Assert the update did not collide with user B's account name

description: A blocked type change shows the 422 message to the user in the edit dialog
steps: Step 1: Open Edit for an account with transactions
Step 2: Force submission of a changed type despite the disabled control
Step 3: Assert the API returns 422
Step 4: Assert the 422 message is displayed in the dialog
Step 5: Assert the dialog remains open so the user can correct the input
Step 6: Assert the account row still shows the original type

description: Account edit dialog is visually consistent with the rest of the accounts page and clearly signals the type lock
steps: Step 1: Open the Accounts page at desktop width and click Edit on an account without transactions
Step 2: Take a screenshot of the edit dialog
Step 3: Verify the fields for name, type, primary currency, notes, and active flag are labeled and aligned
Step 4: Verify the primary action button is visually distinct and the cancel action is secondary
Step 5: Open Edit on an account with transactions
Step 6: Take a screenshot of the dialog
Step 7: Verify the disabled type control is visually distinguishable
Step 8: Verify the lock explanation is readable and not low-contrast
Step 9: Resize to mobile and verify the dialog fields stack without horizontal overflow
Step 10: Verify error messages appear in a readable inline style

description: FilterState includes account_id and the filter row has an account select with an empty all-accounts option
steps: Step 1: Inspect FilterState in resources/js/pages/transactions.tsx and confirm account_id is part of it
Step 2: Open the Transactions page and confirm the existing filter row includes an account select
Step 3: Confirm the select is populated from the accounts already loaded for the transaction form
Step 4: Confirm the select includes an empty option meaning all accounts
Step 5: Confirm the transaction create and edit form's account field was not changed

description: Comprehensive transaction account filter shows only that account's transactions and still works after clearing other filters
steps: Step 1: Seed two accounts for the signed-in user and transactions under each
Step 2: Open the Transactions page
Step 3: Select the first account in the account filter
Step 4: Verify GET /api/transactions is sent with account_id for that account
Step 5: Verify only that account's transactions are listed
Step 6: Apply a category filter and verify both account_id and the category filter are sent
Step 7: Clear the other filters but keep the account filter and verify a second request still sends account_id
Step 8: Verify only that account's transactions are listed again
Step 9: Select the empty all-accounts option and verify the account_id is no longer sent
Step 10: Verify transactions for every account are listed again
Step 11: Select a second account and verify only that account's transactions appear
Step 12: Verify pagination preserves the account filter
Step 13: Verify sorting and searching preserve the account filter
Step 14: Take screenshots of the filtered and unfiltered states as evidence

description: Clearing filters clears the account filter too
steps: Step 1: Open the Transactions page and select an account
Step 2: Apply at least one other filter
Step 3: Use the clear-filters affordance
Step 4: Verify the account select returns to the empty all-accounts option
Step 5: Verify the transactions list shows every account again
Step 6: Verify the URL no longer carries the account query parameter

description: The account filter counts as an active filter for the clear-filters affordance
steps: Step 1: Open the Transactions page with no filters and verify the clear-filters affordance is inactive or hidden
Step 2: Select an account only
Step 3: Verify the clear-filters affordance becomes active or visible
Step 4: Clear filters and verify the affordance returns to inactive or hidden

description: The page reads an account query parameter on load and writes it back when the filter changes
steps: Step 1: Note an account id for the signed-in user
Step 2: Open /transactions?account={id}
Step 3: Verify the page loads with that account selected in the account filter
Step 4: Verify only that account's transactions are listed
Step 5: Change the account filter and verify the URL query parameter is updated
Step 6: Combine ?account={id} with ?period={YYYYMM} and verify both are applied on load
Step 7: Reload the URL and verify the same filter state is restored

description: The transaction create and edit form's account field is unchanged by the filter work
steps: Step 1: Open the Transactions page and open the create form
Step 2: Verify the account field is present and required or optional exactly as before
Step 3: Create a transaction and verify it saves with the chosen account
Step 4: Open the edit form for that transaction and verify the account field still behaves as before
Step 5: Confirm the new filter select is separate from the form field

description: The new account filter select aligns with the existing filter row and controls
steps: Step 1: Open the Transactions page at desktop width
Step 2: Take a screenshot of the filter row
Step 3: Verify the account select matches the height, spacing, and styling of the other filter controls
Step 4: Verify its label or placeholder is clear and translated
Step 5: Verify the empty option reads as all accounts
Step 6: Verify the clear-filters affordance is still discoverable
Step 7: Resize to mobile and verify the filter row wraps without overlap
Step 8: Verify the select is keyboard focusable with a visible focus ring
Step 9: Verify no layout shift occurs when an account is selected
Step 10: Verify the select does not overflow its container at narrow widths

description: Import page shows empty file inputs and no preselected or hardcoded personal filenames
steps: Step 1: Sign in and navigate to the Import page from the navigation
Step 2: Assert the Transactions card has a file input that accepts .json and .csv and is empty
Step 3: Assert the Accounts card has a file input that accepts one or more .json month-sheet files and is empty
Step 4: Assert the Balance sheet card has a file input that accepts one .json file and is empty
Step 5: Assert no personal filename such as gastos_ledger_2025_2026.json, estado_financiero_2025_2026.json, or month_sheets appears anywhere on the page

description: Comprehensive transaction JSON upload through the Import page creates only that user's transactions and reports imported/skipped/errors
steps: Step 1: Add a small synthetic transaction JSON fixture under tests/fixtures with valid fecha, periodo, concepto_code, nested cad/usd/cop value, and comentarios fields
Step 2: Sign in as user A and navigate to the Import page
Step 3: Choose that .json fixture in the Transactions card file input
Step 4: Submit the Transactions card
Step 5: Observe the request is multipart/form-data and contains no file_path, directory, or filename field in the body
Step 6: Verify the success result shows imported, skipped, and errors counts returned by TransactionImportService
Step 7: Navigate to the Transactions page and confirm the expected rows for user A exist with the correct amounts and currency values
Step 8: Confirm rows missing fecha or periodo were skipped and counted in skipped
Step 9: Confirm no rows were created for any other user
Step 10: Verify the uploaded temp file is deleted from storage after parsing
Step 11: Re-submit the same fixture and confirm behavior is deterministic (no partial or duplicated writes beyond service rules)
Step 12: Confirm the API returned a successful status and a readable result payload

description: Comprehensive transaction CSV upload maps cad, usd, cop columns onto the nested value fields and ignores extra columns
steps: Step 1: Add a synthetic transactions CSV fixture under tests/fixtures whose header is fecha,periodo,concepto_code,cad,usd,cop,comentarios
Step 2: Sign in as user A and open the Import page
Step 3: Select the CSV fixture in the Transactions file input and submit
Step 4: Verify the CSV rows are parsed and mapped to the same nested value fields the JSON importer uses
Step 5: Verify imported/skipped/errors counts are shown
Step 6: Navigate to Transactions and confirm the created rows match the CSV values for cad, usd, and cop
Step 7: Add a CSV fixture that also has an unknown extra column and import it
Step 8: Verify the extra column is ignored and the import still succeeds
Step 9: Submit a CSV whose header is missing a required column
Step 10: Verify the API responds 422 with a readable message naming the missing header
Step 11: Verify no rows are created for the rejected CSV
Step 12: Confirm the browser test never POSTs a directory or plan/extracted file_path

description: Comprehensive accounts import accepts one or more uploaded month-sheet JSON files without requiring a directory on disk
steps: Step 1: Add a synthetic month-sheet JSON fixture under tests/fixtures with header.period.value (YYYYMM) and sections.Cuentas.items carrying label plus recorded.cad/usd/cop.value
Step 2: Add a second synthetic month-sheet fixture for a different period
Step 3: Sign in as user A and open the Import page
Step 4: Select both .json month-sheet fixtures in the Accounts card multi-file input
Step 5: Submit the Accounts card
Step 6: Verify the request is multipart upload only with no directory field
Step 7: Verify the existing month-sheet parser processed both files and the result shows imported/skipped/errors
Step 8: Navigate to Accounts and confirm the accounts from the fixtures now exist for user A
Step 9: Open Manage Balances on an imported account and confirm recorded balances match the fixture values
Step 10: Confirm no data was written for any other user
Step 11: Confirm uploaded temp files were deleted after parsing
Step 12: Upload a month-sheet fixture with the wrong top-level shape and verify a 422 with a readable message, not a 500
Step 13: Verify the rejected file created no accounts

description: Comprehensive balance sheet JSON upload is parsed by BalanceSheetImportService from an uploaded file
steps: Step 1: Add a synthetic balance sheet JSON fixture under tests/fixtures as an array of objects with periodo (YYYYMM), activo_value, pasivo_value, and patrimonio_value
Step 2: Sign in as user A and open the Import page
Step 3: Select the fixture in the Balance sheet card file input and submit
Step 4: Verify the request is a multipart upload with no file_path or directory field
Step 5: Verify imported/skipped/errors counts are shown
Step 6: Navigate to the Balance Sheet page and select the imported period
Step 7: Confirm the assets, liabilities, and equity figures match the fixture values
Step 8: Confirm the imported row belongs to user A only
Step 9: Confirm the uploaded temp file is deleted after parsing
Step 10: Upload an invalid JSON document and verify a 422 with a readable message, not a 500
Step 11: Upload a file with a disallowed extension and verify a 422
Step 12: Confirm the rejected uploads created no historical balance sheet rows

description: Submitting an import card with no file is rejected in the browser before calling the API
steps: Step 1: Sign in and open the Import page
Step 2: Leave the Transactions card file input empty and click Submit
Step 3: Verify no network request to the import endpoint is made
Step 4: Verify the user sees a readable validation message asking for a file
Step 5: Repeat for the Accounts card and the Balance sheet card

description: Comprehensive import validation returns 422 with readable messages for invalid JSON, wrong shape, and disallowed extensions and never a 500
steps: Step 1: POST a syntactically invalid JSON file to the transactions import endpoint
Step 2: Assert the response status is 422 and the body contains a readable error message
Step 3: POST a JSON document whose top-level shape is an object instead of an array and assert 422
Step 4: POST a file with a disallowed extension such as .txt to each import card and assert 422
Step 5: POST an accounts month-sheet missing header.period.value and assert 422
Step 6: POST an accounts month-sheet missing sections.Cuentas.items and assert 422
Step 7: POST a balance sheet JSON missing periodo and assert 422
Step 8: POST a balance sheet JSON missing activo_value and assert 422
Step 9: POST a CSV missing the fecha header and assert 422
Step 10: Assert no validation failure returns a 500 status
Step 11: Assert each error message is human readable and does not leak a stack trace
Step 12: Assert none of the rejected requests wrote any rows
Step 13: Assert the HTTP client never received a client-supplied path
Step 14: Run the PHPUnit import feature tests and confirm all pass

description: Import API no longer accepts file_path or directory and rejects any request that names plan/extracted
steps: Step 1: POST a request body with file_path plan/extracted/gastos_ledger_2025_2026.json to the transactions import endpoint
Step 2: Assert the request is rejected and no transactions are imported
Step 3: POST a request body with directory month_sheets to the accounts import endpoint
Step 4: Assert the request is rejected and no accounts are imported
Step 5: POST a request that names any absolute path under plan/extracted to the balance sheet import endpoint
Step 6: Assert it is rejected with a 422 or 403 and no rows are written
Step 7: Search TransactionImportController, AccountImportController, and BalanceSheetImportController for base_path('plan/extracted') and confirm zero matches
Step 8: Search app for any controller that resolves a client-supplied path on disk and confirm none remains
Step 9: Assert the API only reads from the uploaded multipart file
Step 10: Assert plan/extracted files are not modified or deleted by the application
Step 11: Run the security-related import feature tests and confirm they pass
Step 12: Confirm a signed-in attacker cannot read another user's data through the path parameters

description: Uploaded import temp files are stored temporarily, parsed, and deleted
steps: Step 1: Trigger a successful transaction import upload
Step 2: Observe the controller stores the file in a temporary location before parsing
Step 3: Confirm the service reads the temporary file
Step 4: Confirm the temporary file is deleted after the response is built
Step 5: Repeat for accounts and balance sheet imports
Step 6: Assert no uploaded file remains in storage after the requests complete

description: Import through uploads is owner-scoped so a user only ever creates and sees their own data
steps: Step 1: Sign in as user A and import a transaction fixture
Step 2: Sign in as user B and confirm user B cannot see user A's imported transactions
Step 3: Sign in as user B and import a month-sheet fixture
Step 4: Confirm user A cannot see user B's imported accounts or balances
Step 5: Confirm each import statistics endpoint is scoped to the authenticated owner
Step 6: Confirm no import endpoint accepts a user_id from the client
Step 7: Run the owner isolation feature tests and confirm they pass

description: Import page remains reachable from the navigation after the upload change
steps: Step 1: Sign in and locate the Import link in the navigation
Step 2: Confirm the link is present and its label is translated if i18n is active
Step 3: Click it and confirm the Import page loads with all three cards
Step 4: Confirm the route name is still 'import' and the page component is resources/js/pages/import.tsx

description: Synthetic import fixtures exist under tests/fixtures and no personal ledger data is copied from plan/extracted
steps: Step 1: List tests/fixtures and confirm small synthetic transaction, account month-sheet, and balance sheet fixtures exist
Step 2: Confirm the existing tests/fixtures/month_sheets/202501_sample.json is used as a valid month-sheet example
Step 3: Grep the fixtures and tests for gastos_ledger_2025_2026.json, estado_financiero_2025_2026.json, and month_sheets directory POSTs
Step 4: Confirm PHPUnit and Playwright import through uploads of fixtures or through factories instead

description: Import page presents three clearly separated upload cards with empty, accessible file inputs
steps: Step 1: Sign in and open the Import page at desktop width
Step 2: Take a screenshot of the full page
Step 3: Verify the Transactions, Accounts, and Balance sheet cards are visually distinct with clear titles and descriptions
Step 4: Verify each card shows an obvious file-chooser control
Step 5: Verify the Accounts card indicates multiple files may be chosen
Step 6: Verify the allowed extensions are communicated for each card
Step 7: Verify no personal filename hint text is visible
Step 8: Take a screenshot at a narrow mobile width and verify the cards stack without clipping
Step 9: Verify buttons have consistent styling and adequate contrast
Step 10: Verify no empty section, orphaned heading, or placeholder path remains

description: users.locale column is added as a non-null string defaulting to en and existing users migrate to en
steps: Step 1: Inspect the new migration that adds users.locale
Step 2: Assert the column is a string, not nullable, with default en
Step 3: Run the migration on a database with existing users
Step 4: Assert every existing user now has locale en
Step 5: Create a new user without specifying a locale and assert the stored locale is en

description: Locale validation rejects any value other than en or es
steps: Step 1: Sign in and POST a preferences update with locale fr and the current default_currency
Step 2: Assert a 422 validation error
Step 3: Assert the stored locale is unchanged
Step 4: POST locale es and assert success
Step 5: POST locale en and assert success
Step 6: POST an empty locale and assert a validation error
Step 7: Run the feature test that rejects a locale other than en or es

description: Locale is shared on the Inertia auth user next to default_currency
steps: Step 1: Sign in and inspect the shared Inertia auth user props
Step 2: Assert auth.user.locale is present
Step 3: Assert auth.user.default_currency is still present next to it
Step 4: Change the locale in preferences and verify the shared prop updates after the redirect

description: Preferences form gains a language select beside the default currency and saving posts both values
steps: Step 1: Sign in and open the Preferences page
Step 2: Verify a language select is present with exactly English (en) and Spanish (es) options
Step 3: Verify it is positioned beside the existing default currency field
Step 4: Verify the language select shows the current value
Step 5: Choose Spanish and change the default currency, then submit
Step 6: Verify the POST body contains both locale and default_currency
Step 7: Verify a success message is shown
Step 8: Reload the Preferences page and verify both values persisted
Step 9: Assert no other locale values are offered
Step 10: Assert the available currencies remain CAD, USD, and COP only

description: Comprehensive language switch to Spanish changes navigation and preferences and persists on later visits
steps: Step 1: Sign in as a user whose locale is en
Step 2: Open Preferences and confirm the UI is English
Step 3: Select Spanish and save
Step 4: Verify the redirect renders navigation in Spanish
Step 5: Verify the Preferences page strings are Spanish
Step 6: Verify document.documentElement.lang is es
Step 7: Navigate to the dashboard and verify its chrome is Spanish
Step 8: Navigate to the accounts and transactions pages and verify their chrome is Spanish
Step 9: Sign out and sign back in
Step 10: Verify the UI is still Spanish without opening Preferences
Step 11: Verify no manual reload beyond Inertia's normal redirect was needed
Step 12: Confirm user-entered data such as account and category names is not translated

description: Choosing English returns the UI to English
steps: Step 1: Sign in as a user whose locale is es
Step 2: Verify the UI is Spanish
Step 3: Open Preferences and select English
Step 4: Save and verify the redirect renders English navigation
Step 5: Verify document.documentElement.lang is en
Step 6: Reload and verify the UI stays English

description: Comprehensive i18n coverage: navigation, footer, dashboard, accounts, transactions, categories, reconciliation, period balances, balance sheet, preferences, settings, import, exchange rates, income, budgets, reports, and auth screens are translated
steps: Step 1: Confirm react-i18next and its i18next peer are installed and initialized
Step 2: Confirm catalogs exist in resources/js/locales/en and resources/js/locales/es
Step 3: Set the user locale to es
Step 4: Verify navigation and footer strings are Spanish on every authenticated page
Step 5: Verify the dashboard page is Spanish
Step 6: Verify the accounts page and account detail page are Spanish
Step 7: Verify the transactions page is Spanish
Step 8: Verify the categories page is Spanish
Step 9: Verify the reconciliation page is Spanish
Step 10: Verify the period balances page is Spanish
Step 11: Verify the balance sheet page is Spanish
Step 12: Verify the preferences and settings pages are Spanish
Step 13: Verify the import and exchange rates pages are Spanish
Step 14: Verify the income, budgets, and reports pages are Spanish
Step 15: Verify the login, register, password, and two-factor auth screens are Spanish
Step 16: Switch back to en and spot-check several of the same pages in English

description: The document documentElement lang attribute is set to en or es from the active language
steps: Step 1: Sign in with locale en and assert document.documentElement.lang is en
Step 2: Change the locale to es and assert document.documentElement.lang becomes es
Step 3: Change back to en and assert it becomes en
Step 4: Assert no other value is ever set

description: English catalog is the fallback so a missing Spanish key shows the English string, not the key
steps: Step 1: Locate a key that exists in the English catalog but intentionally is absent from the Spanish catalog
Step 2: Set the locale to es and render the component that uses it
Step 3: Assert the English string is displayed
Step 4: Assert the raw translation key is not displayed
Step 5: Assert i18n does not fall back to a different language than en

description: User-entered data is never passed through the translation catalogs
steps: Step 1: Create an account named with an English word and a category named with a Spanish word
Step 2: Add notes and a transaction comment in mixed languages
Step 3: Switch the UI to Spanish and inspect those values on every page where they appear
Step 4: Assert the account name, category name, notes, and transaction comments are shown exactly as stored

description: Comprehensive exchange-rates:fetch command persists USD-base quotes from latest.json and is idempotent across runs on the same day
steps: Step 1: Configure services.openexchangerates.app_id from OPENEXCHANGERATES_APP_ID and document it in .env.example
Step 2: Fake the HTTP client so the command receives a latest.json payload with rates.CAD and rates.COP
Step 3: Run php artisan exchange-rates:fetch
Step 4: Assert one global snapshot row is written with source openexchangerates, user_id null, and the response date
Step 5: Assert cad_per_usd equals rates.CAD and cop_per_usd equals rates.COP
Step 6: Assert every other currency in the payload is ignored
Step 7: Run the command a second time on the same day with the same payload
Step 8: Assert there is still exactly one global snapshot row for that date
Step 9: Run again with updated quotes and assert the same row is updated idempotently
Step 10: Assert the command's update-or-create matches rate_date + source + null user_id rather than relying on a unique index alone
Step 11: Assert no live API call is made in tests
Step 12: Confirm the command reads the app id from config services.openexchangerates.app_id

description: exchange-rates:fetch logs a warning and exits successfully with no row when the app id is missing

Step 2: Run php artisan exchange-rates:fetch
Step 3: Assert the command logs a warning
Step 4: Assert it exits with a successful status code
Step 5: Assert it does not throw an exception
Step 6: Assert no snapshot row is written

description: Comprehensive exchange-rates:fetch HTTP or payload failure logs the error, exits non-zero, and writes no partial row
steps: Step 1: Fake the HTTP client to return a 500 response
Step 2: Run php artisan exchange-rates:fetch
Step 3: Assert the command logs the error
Step 4: Assert the exit code is non-zero
Step 5: Assert no snapshot row was written
Step 6: Fake the HTTP client to return a 200 with a malformed payload missing rates.CAD
Step 7: Run the command again
Step 8: Assert the error is logged and the exit code is non-zero
Step 9: Assert no partial row was written
Step 10: Fake a payload where rates.CAD is present but rates.COP is missing and assert the same failure behavior
Step 11: Assert a subsequent successful run still writes exactly one row
Step 12: Confirm the command only calls latest.json and never historical, time-series, or convert endpoints

description: Comprehensive manual snapshot upsert creates or updates the current user's row per date
steps: Step 1: Sign in as user A and open the exchange-rates page
Step 2: Locate the manual entry form separate from period selection
Step 3: Assert it asks for a date, CAD per 1 USD, and COP per 1 USD only
Step 4: Submit a date with both quotes greater than zero

Step 6: Submit the same date again with different quotes
Step 7: Assert the same user row is updated, not duplicated
Step 8: Submit with a missing quote and assert a 422
Step 9: Submit with a zero or negative quote and assert a 422
Step 10: Assert the form never asks for a CAD/COP cross rate
Step 11: Assert another user's manual row for the same date is separate
Step 12: Confirm the cross rate is only ever derived

description: A manual snapshot does not overwrite the global fetched row for the same date

Step 3: Assert the global row's cad_per_usd and cop_per_usd are unchanged
Step 4: Assert the user's manual row exists separately
Step 5: Assert both rows are visible to that user where applicable

description: Comprehensive period assignment: a snapshot assigned to a YYYYMM period drives ExchangeRate::forPeriod conversions
steps: Step 1: Create a global snapshot for a date in 202501 with cad_per_usd 1.36 and cop_per_usd 4000
Step 2: Sign in and assign that snapshot to period 202501
Step 3: Assert the exchange_rates row for 202501 has the required snapshot_id set
Step 4: Call ExchangeRate::forPeriod('202501') and assert it returns the owner's row
Step 5: Assert conversion methods read the linked snapshot
Step 6: Assign a different snapshot to 202501 and assert it replaces the previous assignment
Step 7: Assert the previously assigned snapshot row still exists and was not deleted
Step 8: Create a manual snapshot with distinct quotes and assign it to 202501
Step 9: Assert forPeriod('202501') now converts with the manual snapshot quotes
Step 10: Assert the picker lists global fetched snapshots and that user's manual snapshots
Step 11: Assert the picker date filter defaults to dates inside that month
Step 12: Assert a nearby date such as the last day of the month can be chosen
Step 13: Assert another user's assignment for 202501 does not affect this user
Step 14: Run the feature tests for period assignment and confirm they pass

description: Comprehensive conversion directions follow the USD-base quote convention
steps: Step 1: Assign a snapshot with cad_per_usd 1.36 and cop_per_usd 4000 to the period
Step 2: Assert 100 USD converts to 136.00 CAD using amount * cad_per_usd
Step 3: Assert 136 CAD converts to 100.00 USD using amount / cad_per_usd
Step 4: Assert 100 USD converts to 400000 COP using amount * cop_per_usd
Step 5: Assert 400000 COP converts to 100.00 USD using amount / cop_per_usd
Step 6: Assert copToCad uses amount / cop_per_usd * cad_per_usd
Step 7: Assert cadToCop uses amount / cad_per_usd * cop_per_usd
Step 8: Assert toCad returns the amount unchanged for CAD
Step 9: Assert toCad multiplies by cad_per_usd for USD
Step 10: Assert toCad converts COP through the cross rate
Step 11: Assert a zero quote returns 0 for a conversion that would divide by it
Step 12: Assert usdToCad multiplies by cad_per_usd rather than dividing by usd_cad
Step 13: Update the test that expected division and confirm it now expects multiplication
Step 14: Confirm derived usd_cop = cop_per_usd, usd_cad = cad_per_usd, and cad_cop = cop_per_usd / cad_per_usd

description: COP to CAD uses the derived cross rate rather than a separately typed CAD/COP input
steps: Step 1: Assign a snapshot with cad_per_usd 1.36 and cop_per_usd 4000
Step 2: Convert 400000 COP to CAD and assert the result is 136.00
Step 3: Assert the result equals amount / cop_per_usd * cad_per_usd
Step 4: Confirm the exchange rates page has no CAD/COP input
Step 5: Confirm the API does not accept cad_cop as input

description: A zero quote returns 0 for a conversion that would divide by it
steps: Step 1: Create a snapshot with cad_per_usd 0 and cop_per_usd 4000
Step 2: Convert CAD to USD and assert the result is 0
Step 3: Convert CAD to COP and assert the result is 0 or otherwise does not divide by zero
Step 4: Assert no exception or infinity is produced

description: Derived accessors keep usd_cop, usd_cad, and cad_cop names for existing API payloads

Step 3: Assert usd_cop equals cop_per_usd
Step 4: Assert usd_cad equals cad_per_usd
Step 5: Assert cad_cop equals cop_per_usd / cad_per_usd
Step 6: Assert the old three numbers are not accepted as user input anymore

description: Comprehensive migration backfills existing exchange_rates rows into manual snapshots and points each period at its snapshot
steps: Step 1: Seed existing exchange_rates rows for multiple users and periods with known usd_cop, usd_cad, and cad_cop values
Step 2: Run the migration
Step 3: Assert a manual snapshot is created for each existing row owned by that row's user_id
Step 4: Assert rate_date is the last calendar day of the row's YYYYMM period
Step 5: Assert cop_per_usd equals the stored usd_cop

Step 8: Assert each period row's snapshot_id points at its created snapshot
Step 9: Assert rows with identical quotes for the same user and date reuse one snapshot
Step 10: Assert rows with differing quotes for the same user and date each get their own snapshot
Step 11: Assert the foreign key is enforced after the backfill
Step 12: After migration, assert usd_cop, usd_cad, and cad_cop columns are dropped from exchange_rates once nothing reads them as columns

description: ExchangeRate::forPeriod still returns the owner's row and conversion methods use the linked snapshot

description: Comprehensive missing-rate behavior: a period with no assignment does not synthesize 4400, 0.75, or 3000
